title: Your website doesn't need a cloud bill: what hosting actually costs

chapters.headline: The expensive assumption
points: The usual assumption: a business website belongs on AWS or Azure — reasonable, and expensive
The alternative: site files in a GitHub repository, delivered by Cloudflare — $0 a month in hosting
The domain costs about $10 a year; this site's cost $10.46
chapters.takeaway: Every price in this edition is as published on October 7, 2026 — check the vendor's current page before you budget.

chapters.headline: Most business websites are just pages
points: Most business websites: pages, articles, a contact form, maybe a newsletter signup — written once, read many times
No server chewing on computation, no database cluster, nothing that needs to stay awake all night
AWS and Azure are built, brilliantly, for the other kind: applications, backends, compute that scales
chapters.takeaway: Putting a brochure-and-articles website on a big cloud is like leasing a delivery fleet to drive one van.

chapters.headline: The big clouds meter success
points: Azure Static Web Apps: $0 free tier, then $9 per app per month; 100 GB of bandwidth included, then $0.20 per GB
AWS: roughly $1–3 a month for the basics, assembled from parts — and the firewall is separate: $5 per rule set plus $1 per rule
A terabyte month, modeled: still $0 on Cloudflare Pages; roughly $189 on Azure — $9 for the app plus about $180 of bandwidth overage
chapters.takeaway: The big clouds meter the one thing a successful website uses most: bandwidth.

chapters.headline: Rent forever, and the builder keeps your site
points: GoDaddy's builder: advertised around $9.99 a month, renewing around $12.99; a .com renews at roughly $19–23 a year
A site built in GoDaddy's builder cannot be taken elsewhere as-is — leaving means rebuilding
Namecheap is the fairest of the traditional hosts: $1.98 a month for the first year, renewing at $4.88, privacy protection included free — still rent, forever, for a mostly idle server
chapters.takeaway: The GitHub-plus-Cloudflare combination is not a cheaper rental. It removes the rental.

chapters.headline: Databases and video, same pattern
points: Databases: Cloudflare's D1 starts with a generous free allowance — 5 GB of storage; Azure Cosmos DB has a lifetime free tier (1,000 RU/s, 25 GB); the smallest always-on AWS RDS database runs about $12 a month
Video: Cloudflare Stream is $5 per 1,000 minutes stored plus $1 per 1,000 minutes delivered, no bandwidth charges on top
Azure retired its media services in 2024; AWS assembles video from three separately metered parts; GoDaddy and Namecheap have no streaming product at all
chapters.takeaway: At every layer the pattern holds: bundled whole products, small versions tied to a rental, or separately metered parts.

chapters.headline: Where the big clouds are the right answer
points: A real application backend — persistent servers, heavy databases, private networking — belongs on AWS or Azure
A compliance regime, a contract that names a specific cloud, or committed cloud spend settles the question by itself
This site, on the free combination: 100 out of 100 on AI-search readiness checks, 90% on independent SEO checks, $0 a month plus the $10.46-a-year domain
chapters.takeaway: Host the project that crosses the line on the big cloud — and keep your website where websites belong.

chapters.headline: Take the toolkit, or take a hand
points: The method is packaged and published free, under an open-source license: website-forge, linked in the article
It walks your own AI assistant through the same process: spec first, wireframes before pages, staging before live, verified by screenshots
Starting a business? The startup support package sets up domain, website, and professional email properly from day one
chapters.takeaway: The first conversation costs the same as the hosting: nothing.
